answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 24 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the vine solution is checked at the walnut gate and logged, the nebula audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch as a result pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 6 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
